note: Reel 13: Mosquito Magnet. Why mosquitoes pick some people: not sweet blood; breath, heat, then skin smell; the 2022 Cell study (64 people in nylon stockings, dengue mosquitoes choosing two at a time, Subject 33 about 100 times more attractive than last place, skin rich in certain acids, mosquitoes with a damaged sense of smell still found the magnets, the same over three years). Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0. Numbers are written as words so the display words match the voice's tokens one to one. Spelling for the voice: 'meters' (the American voice reads it as written; the screen says METRES). Variants test the risky words: s07b spells dengue in phonemes, s08b spells Subject (the noun) in phonemes; the checks pick. Facts: docs/research.md.

lines.text: Mosquitoes love some people a hundred times more than others.
If that's you, it isn't your sweet blood.
They pick you before they've tasted a drop.
They follow your breath from ten meters away, then your heat.
But everyone breathes, and everyone's warm. So why you?
In a New York lab, sixty-four people wore nylon stockings on their arms.
Then dengue mosquitoes chose between them, two at a time.
Then dengue mosquitoes chose between them, two at a time.
lines.text_kokoro: Then [dengue](/dˈɛŋɡi/) mosquitoes chose between them, two at a time.

lines.text: One volunteer kept winning. Subject thirty-three.
One volunteer kept winning. Subject thirty-three.
A hundred times more attractive than last place.
Their skin made far more of certain acids, and mosquitoes follow that smell.
Even mosquitoes with a damaged sense of smell still found them.
And three years later, the magnets were still magnets.
So if they always pick you, they'll pick you next year too.

ref_text: The night was warm and very quiet.
